about: The exorcism at the Entrance to Hades, done right, in Zork's order and to its clock (LLD-ROOM, BELL-F, HOT-BELL-F, CANDLES-FCN, BLACK-BOOK, GHOSTS-F, GATE-PSEUDO): down the hole in the Altar's floor to the Cave and its stairs, the evil spirits barring the gate, untouchable, jeering at whoever talks to them, and the gate's invisible force turning everyone back; the exorcism asked for, and the ceremony wanted; the bell rung grows red hot and falls, and the candles in hand fall and go out, while the wraiths reel; the hot bell cannot be taken or rung; the candles taken up again and lit with a match while they reel make them cower; the black book read while they cower drives them off for good, and the way through the gate is open, to the Land of the Dead.

expect.words: West of House
You are standing in an open field west of a white house, with a boarded front door.
There is a small mailbox here.
Taken.
Taken.
Taken.
Cave
This is a tiny cave with entrances west and north, and a dark, forbidding staircase leading down.
Entrance to Hades
You are outside a large gateway, on which is inscribed
Abandon every hope all ye who enter here!
The gate is open; through it you can see a desolation, with a pile of mangled bodies in one corner. Thousands of voices, lamenting some hideous fate, can be heard.
The way through the gate is barred by evil spirits, who jeer at your attempts to pass.

The spirits crowd the gateway, pale and thin as smoke and in no way friendly, with faces that are mostly mouth. They drift back and forth across the way through, jeering, plucking at the air where you stand, and whenever you take a step toward the gate there are suddenly a great many more of them. They have been here a very long time, and they intend to stay.

It is a gateway of black iron, very large, its two leaves standing wide open as if nobody had ever had any reason to close them. Over it the inscription is cut deep. Through it lies a grey desolation, and the way through is, for all that it is open, not at all inviting. The air in the gateway has a faint shimmer, like heat over a road.
Abandon every hope all ye who enter here!

Through the gate, in one corner of the desolation beyond, lies a pile of mangled bodies, heaped as carelessly as firewood. None of them is moving, and none of them looks as if it ever expected to be here.
Thousands of voices, lamenting some hideous fate. You listen for a while, and wish you had not; it is the kind of thing that stays with you.
Some invisible force prevents you from passing through the gate.
Some invisible force prevents you from passing through the gate.
Some invisible force prevents you from passing through the gate.
The spirits jeer loudly and ignore you.
How can you attack a spirit with material objects?
You seem unable to interact with these spirits.
You must perform the ceremony.

The bell suddenly becomes red hot and falls to the ground. The wraiths, as if paralyzed, stop their jeering and slowly turn to face you. On their ashen faces, the expression of a long-forgotten terror takes shape.
In your confusion, the candles drop to the ground (and they are out).
The bell glows a dull red from lip to handle, and the air above it shivers. The wooden handle has charred black. It ticks faintly as it cools, very slowly, in no hurry to be picked up.
The bell is very hot and cannot be taken.
The bell is too hot to reach.
Taken.
One of the matches starts to burn.
The candles are lit.
The flames flicker wildly and appear to dance. The earth beneath your feet trembles, and your legs nearly buckle beneath you. The spirits cower at your unearthly power.

Each word of the prayer reverberates through the hall in a deafening confusion. As the last word fades, a voice, loud and commanding, speaks: "Begone, fiends!" A heart-stopping scream fills the cavern, and the spirits, sensing a greater power, flee through the walls.

Land of the Dead

You have entered the Land of the Living Dead. Thousands of lost souls can be heard weeping and moaning. In the corner are stacked the remains of dozens of previous adventurers less fortunate than yourself. A passage exits to the north.
Lying in one corner of the room is a beautifully carved crystal skull. It appears to be grinning at you rather nastily.
